newsitem.title: FRANCE: French beet planters support gene-modified crops.
newsitem.headline: French beet planters support gene-modified crops.

text.p: French sugar beet planters said on Thursday that unless France and the European Union encourage the production of gene-modified crops, they risk losing out to other producers.

"Public authorities must launch a large information campaign to balance out scientific progress against (consumer) fears. Otherwise France and the EU will lose to others that sector of development," director general of the CGB planters federation Alain Jeanroy told a news conference.
He said better information about the safety and benefits of gene-altered crops was paramount.
The EU has already allowed member states to import gene-modified soy but has yet to approve imports of gene-altered maize.

But the first shipments of new crop U.S. soybeans to Europe, thought to contain gene-altered beans, have sparked protests from environmental and consumer groups that fear the modified beans could be a risk to health.
Three EU scientific and expert groups are due to report in December on the safety of approving the sale to the EU of gene-modified maize.
